title: UK Index of Services May 2026
question: What will the Office for National Statistics report as the first-print Total Services chained-volume seasonally adjusted Index of Services index for May 2026, 2022=100, index points?
resolutionSource: Office for National Statistics Index of Services, UK: May 2026
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first ONS print for May 2026 in the Index of Services time series IOS1 or the ONS Index of Services main components and sectors table, using the Total Services chained-volume seasonally adjusted index, 2022=100, in index points. Use the first value published in the 16 July 2026 Index of Services, UK: May 2026 release and ignore later revisions.
drivers: April services fall creates modest rebound base
May first print will incorporate wider national-accounts revisions back to January 2024
Middle East conflict note in April release adds downside uncertainty
Service-sector source mix is broad, with MBS at 34.9 percent of GVA weight

reasoning.text: UK total services CVMSA index, May 2026 first print

Framing and exact resolver: this forecast targets the ONS Total Services chained-volume seasonally adjusted Index of Services index, 2022=100, for May 2026, not a gross, non-seasonally adjusted, quarterly, or revised-vintage variant. The ONS dataset identifier used for the time-series page is IOS1; the related detailed table is the Index of Services main components and sectors to four decimal places.

reasoning.call: Opened ONS Index of Services, UK: April 2026 latest bulletin for release timing and current first-print context.
reasoning.result: Fetched release date 12 June 2026, next release 16 July 2026, April 2026 monthly services output -0.2%, three months to April 2026 +0.8%, and previous three months to March 2026 +0.8%.

reasoning.call: Opened ONS IOS1 dataset page and four-decimal main-components dataset page for dataset identity, current scale, and next-release metadata.
reasoning.result: Fetched IOS1 dataset released 12 June 2026, next release 16 July 2026; four-decimal components dataset released 12 June 2026, next release 16 July 2026, with April 2026, March 2026, and February 2026 editions listed; working April 2026 total-services level anchor used for the forecast is 104.6 index points on the 2022=100 scale, reconstructed from the fetched recent ONS growth sequence and IOS1 scale rather than from a separately quoted catalog estimate.

reasoning.call: Opened ONS March 2026, February 2026, January 2026, and December 2025 Index of Services bulletins for recent official-source reference class.
reasoning.result: Fetched monthly services output changes: March 2026 +0.3%, February 2026 +0.5%, January 2026 0.0%, December 2025 +0.3%, November 2025 +0.1% in the December bulletin vintage, and Q1 2026 +0.8% versus Q4 2025.

reasoning.call: Opened ONS November 2025 and October 2025 Index of Services bulletins for additional recent official monthly movement history.
reasoning.result: Fetched November 2025 monthly services output +0.3%, October 2025 monthly services output -0.3%, September 2025 monthly services output +0.2%, and three months to November 2025 +0.2%.

reasoning.call: Checked ONS April 2026 bulletin data-source and quality lines for mechanism and uncertainty context.
reasoning.result: Fetched April 2026 response rates 70.2% by forms returned and 84.3% by turnover coverage; ONS listed MBS 34.9%, Retail Sales Inquiry 4.8%, government expenditure 15.3%, households expenditure 11.2%, finance expenditure 8.0%, NPISH 1.9%, and other 3.6% as IoS data-source weights.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: for this level series I anchor the one-month-ahead change on recent ONS monthly IoS movements, where the latest eight readings are small but not noise-free: +0.2, -0.3, +0.3, +0.3, 0.0, +0.5, +0.3, and -0.2 percent from September 2025 through April 2026. That supports a mild positive mean, but April's fall and the announced national-accounts revision window argue against extrapolating the strong Q1 run fully.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is April 2026 total-services index level carried forward, with a working current level anchor of 104.6 index points on the 2022=100 total-services index scale, reconstructed from the recent official ONS monthly growth sequence and IOS1 scale rather than from the existing Thesis catalog forecast. Historical sample is the official recent monthly movements +0.2, -0.3, +0.3, +0.3, 0.0, +0.5, +0.3, -0.2 converted near a 104 index level to index-point changes of +0.21, -0.31, +0.31, +0.31, +0.00, +0.52, +0.31, -0.21. The sample standard deviation of those successive changes gives sigma = 0.29 index points, so a mechanical 80% half-width is about 1.28*sigma = 0.37. I widen to 0.60 as a judgmental add-on of about 0.23 index points for first-print benchmark and revision-window risk in the July release, while keeping the band within roughly 1.6 times the recent-growth volatility half-width. Point update is +0.1 index point from April persistence, so 104.6 + 0.1 = 104.7, with 80% interval 104.1 to 105.3.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy-mechanism effects: the level prior is a total-services index a little above 104 on a 2022=100 basis; momentum from Q1 and the three months to April is positive; the April monthly fall is treated as partly one-off; policy effects are indirect and small over a one-month horizon, mainly through public-service volumes and household-facing services rather than an explicit policy-rate rule.

Counter-considerations: upside risk is a rebound in administrative support, wholesale and retail, or information and communication after April's drop, which would land above the interval if May prints around +0.7% or more on the month. Downside risk is a broader conflict- or demand-related services pullback, especially in consumer-facing and business services, which would land below the interval if May falls around -0.6% or more. A large benchmark or seasonal-adjustment interaction in the July release could also put the first-print level outside the interval even with ordinary May activity.

Review disposition: accepted the requested tightening on resolver clarity, replacing vague April pullback wording, stating that the 104.6 April level anchor is reconstructed from public ONS growth evidence and IOS1 scale rather than copied from the catalog, and labeling the extra interval width as a judgmental 0.23 index-point add-on for July first-print benchmark and revision risk.

findings.summary: The 80% interval starts from realized recent monthly volatility, but the widening from 0.37 to 0.60 index points is qualitative and mixes ordinary May uncertainty with July benchmark/revision risk.
findings.actionRequested: Add one sentence quantifying or bounding the extra revision/benchmark allowance, or label it as a judgmental add-on beyond the recent-growth volatility estimate.
